name: Sonivex-AD
description: An acoustically active meta-material panel produced by Tessera Materials, using a lattice of micro-resonator cavities tuned at fabrication to target specific frequency ranges, with secondary piezo-actuator layers that can dynamically shift resonator geometry under electronic control to actively dampen or amplify sound in real time. Sonivex-AD can switch from a near-anechoic absorption profile to a directional amplification mode within 200ms, making it uniquely dual-purpose. Panels are typically 12mm thick and can tile seamlessly.
story_hooks: A Sonivex-AD-lined room was used for a meeting that left no electronic trace — but the panels themselves may have recorded acoustic stress patterns in their resonator wear.
Someone has flipped a building's Sonivex-AD panels to amplification mode and is broadcasting sound from a private conversation into the street.
A character needs to cross a room lined with Sonivex-AD in dampening mode — complete silence means any guard inside will hear nothing, but it also means they won't hear anyone coming either.
